hero.title: ERISA Fiduciary Governance & Committee Support for Retirement Plan Sponsors
hero.subtitle: Independent guidance that strengthens your fiduciary process and helps protect your organization.

blocks.text: Serving as a retirement plan fiduciary means more than selecting investments. ERISA requires plan sponsors to monitor investments, evaluate service providers, document decisions, and always act in the best interests of plan participants.

PointOak Retirement Advisors provides independent ERISA fiduciary support that helps retirement plan committees build a documented, repeatable fiduciary process. As a fee-only, SEC-registered investment advisor, we serve as either a 3(21) co-fiduciary or 3(38) investment manager, while also supporting governance, compliance, investment oversight, and committee documentation.

sections.title: How ERISA Fiduciary Governance & Committee Support Works

blocks.text: Every retirement plan has different governance needs. Some committees want to retain investment authority while receiving expert guidance. Others prefer to delegate investment decisions to a discretionary fiduciary.

PointOak helps plan sponsors determine the appropriate fiduciary structure while integrating investment monitoring, provider benchmarking, committee governance, and ERISA compliance into one documented process.

Our approach combines quarterly investment reviews, fiduciary documentation, committee support, and ongoing monitoring so your retirement plan remains aligned with both participant interests and regulatory expectations.

items.q: What is fiduciary support for a retirement plan?

a.text: Fiduciary support helps retirement plan sponsors fulfill their responsibilities under ERISA by providing guidance on investment oversight, governance, compliance, documentation, and ongoing monitoring.

Depending on your needs, fiduciary support may include acting as a 3(21) co-fiduciary, serving as a 3(38) investment manager, assisting with committee governance, conducting fee benchmarking, maintaining fiduciary documentation, and helping monitor investments throughout the year.

items.q: What is the difference between a 3(21) and a 3(38) fiduciary?

a.text: A 3(21) fiduciary provides investment advice while the plan sponsor retains final decision-making authority. A 3(38) fiduciary assumes discretionary authority to select, monitor, and replace plan investments.

Both models help strengthen fiduciary oversight, but they offer different levels of responsibility and delegation. PointOak serves as both a 3(21) investment fiduciary and 3(38) investment manager depending on your organization's governance preferences.

items.q: What is a Virtual Fiduciary File?

a.text: A Virtual Fiduciary File is a centralized repository that stores committee minutes, investment reports, benchmarking studies, governance documents, fiduciary decisions, and supporting documentation.
Maintaining organized records helps demonstrate a prudent fiduciary process and provides an audit-ready history of your retirement plan's oversight.

items.q: Why is documentation so important under ERISA?

a.text: ERISA evaluates the fiduciary process as much as the investment results.

Documenting committee discussions, investment decisions, provider evaluations, benchmarking studies, and ongoing monitoring demonstrates that fiduciaries followed a prudent, repeatable process designed to serve participants' best interests.
